title: Independence of the compactification and the cocycle condition
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be admissible and $f:X\to Y$ separated of finite type with $Y$
qcqs. For compactifications $c_a=(j_a:X\to Z_a,\ p_a:Z_a\to Y)$ write
$Rf_!^{c_a}=Rp_{a*}j_{a!}$ on $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$. For any two
compactifications $c_1,c_2$ there is an isomorphism
$\phi_{c_2,c_1}:Rf_!^{c_1}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_!^{c_2}$, obtained from the
refinement isomorphisms through any common dense refinement, which is
independent of the common refinement chosen and satisfies
$\phi_{c,c}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\phi_{c_3,c_2}\circ\phi_{c_2,c_1}=\phi_{c_3,c_1}$.

proof.text: Put $F_c=Rp_*j_!$ using [def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek-compactification], with source restricted to $\Loc(\Dctf)$ and ambient derived target. Use the coherent compositor $\kappa$ of [lem-sfb-module-derived-compositor-coherence] and the natural normalized arrows $e_h:j_!\to Rh_*j\prime_!$ of [lem-sfb-normalized-open-refinement-coherence]. These are the compositor and the refinement maps $e_h$ (adjoint of $\theta_h^{-1}$) constructed in [def-sf-comp-refinement-data].

For $h:d\to c$ with $d$ dense, [det-nagata-refinement-morphisms](1) gives properness. Apply [lem-sfb-qcqs-proper-open-boundary-vanishing] with $S=Y$, $U=X$ and the two compactification structure maps. Thus $i^*Rh_*j\prime_!K=0$ on the closed complement of $j$. By [lem-sfb-condensed-support-derived-localization], also $i^*j_!K=0$ and the open/closed restrictions jointly detect isomorphisms. Use $r_h:j^*Rh_*\simeq j\prime^*$ from [lem-sfb-identity-open-derived-restriction]; under $r_h$ and the open units, $j^*e_h$ is $1_K$ by Step 1. Both restrictions are therefore invertible, so $e_h$ is invertible.

source.place: Dense replacement and Refinement isomorphisms: general-base boundary argument

proof.text: Define $\rho_h=\kappa_{p,h}^{-1}Rp_*(e_h):F_c\xrightarrow{\sim}F_d$. Substitute $\kappa_{h,k}e_{hk}=Rh_*(e_k)e_h$ from [lem-sfb-normalized-open-refinement-coherence] in this formula. Naturality moves $Rp_*(e_h)$ past the compositor; associativity in [lem-sfb-module-derived-compositor-coherence] identifies the two remaining threefold compositors. Hence $\rho_{hk}=\rho_k\rho_h$. The two unit laws give $\rho_1=1$.

source.place: Refinement isomorphisms: transport of the normalized composition law

proof.text: Choose a common dense refinement $d$ of $c_1,c_2$, with maps $h_1,h_2$, by [det-nagata-refinement-common-dense]. Put $\phi_{c_2,c_1}=\rho_{h_2}^{-1}\rho_{h_1}:F_{c_1}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{c_2}$. Reflections of the boundary condition under composition are the explicit equations of [det-nagata-definition-refinement]. No density of either $c_a$ is needed.

For another choice $d\prime$, choose a common dense $d\prime\prime$ of $d,d\prime$ by [det-nagata-refinement-common-dense], with maps $k,k\prime$. Uniqueness in [det-nagata-refinement-morphisms](3), applied to the dense source $d\prime\prime$, gives $h_ak=h\prime_ak\prime$. Step 3 and cancellation give
$$\rho_{h_2}^{-1}\rho_{h_1}=(\rho_k\rho_{h_2})^{-1}(\rho_k\rho_{h_1})=\rho_{h_2k}^{-1}\rho_{h_1k}=\rho_{h\prime_2k\prime}^{-1}\rho_{h\prime_1k\prime}=\rho_{h\prime_2}^{-1}\rho_{h\prime_1}.$$
This proves independence, including the projection maps.

Use one common dense refinement of three compactifications from [det-nagata-refinement-common-dense]. Independence gives
$$\phi_{c_3,c_2}\phi_{c_2,c_1}=(\rho_{h_3}^{-1}\rho_{h_2})(\rho_{h_2}^{-1}\rho_{h_1})=\rho_{h_3}^{-1}\rho_{h_1}=\phi_{c_3,c_1}.$$
For identity use the same dense projection twice: $\rho_h^{-1}\rho_h=1$, even for nondense $c$. All formulas are equalities of natural transformations.

lean.statement: theorem compactification_coherence_cocycle (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (_hΛ : IsLocalizingAdmissibleCoefficient ℓ Λ) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace Y] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y] (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] : ∃ φ : ∀ c₁ c₂ : Compactification.BoundaryCompactification f, compactificationLocalizingCandidate Λ c₁ ≅ compactificationLocalizingCandidate Λ c₂, (∀ (c : Compactification.BoundaryCompactification f) (d : Compactification.DenseBoundaryCompactification f) (h : d.obj ⟶ c) (K : (localizingClosureProEtale Λ X).FullSubcategory), IsIso (compactificationRefinementComponent Λ h K.obj)) ∧ (∀ (c₁ c₂ : Compactification.BoundaryCompactification f) (d : Compactification.DenseBoundaryCompactification f) (h₁ : d.obj ⟶ c₁) (h₂ : d.obj ⟶ c₂) (K : (localizingClosureProEtale Λ X).FullSubcategory), (φ c₁ c₂).hom.app K ≫ compactificationRefinementComponent Λ h₂ K.obj = compactificationRefinementComponent Λ h₁ K.obj) ∧ (∀ c : Compactification.BoundaryCompactification f, φ c c = Iso.refl _) ∧ (∀ c₁ c₂ c₃ : Compactification.BoundaryCompactification f, φ c₁ c₂ ≪≫ φ c₂ c₃ = φ c₁ c₃)
lean.note: The source-restricted candidate abbreviates the existing unbounded module-object composite. The canonical refinement component is Rp_* of the recorded localizingRefinementMap, followed by the inverse recorded derived compositor and the proper triangle equality. The theorem existentially supplies natural isomorphisms, with normalization against every common dense refinement, identity and cocycle equations. No density is assumed for the two compared compactifications, and no localizing-target preservation is assumed.
